message.reasoning_content: Describe kernel: row sum of 128 cols per row, sequential float32 accumulation. Input: large ±w values (1-32 × 2^20, so up to ~33M) plus small 0.25-0.75 values. Reference sums in real arithmetic. Per-row true sum: w and -w cancel exactly (same integers permuted), so reference = sum of 64 small values ≈ up to 48. But float32 sequential summation: large values cancel only if exact; w values are exact in fp32 (integers up to 33*2^20, exactly representable). Sums of large magnitudes may accumulate rounding, error relative to small final value. E denominator uses reference norm (~ sqrt(64*~12²)≈96), E≤0.1 means error budget ~9.6 in L2 over 64 rows... actually errors could be large: each fp32 addition of magnitude ~2^25 values rounds to ulp ~2^2=4. Accumulated error across 128 additions could be hundreds, then small additions lost. Sequential order after permutation mixes large and small. Risk: catastrophic cancellation — small entries (0.25) are far below ulp of running sum (~millions), so small contributions vanish entirely unless large terms cancel first. Since w and -w are same set per row, they cancel exactly in exact arithmetic but in fp32 partial sums with rounding, residual error remains large relative to 48. Actually large terms: 32 positive w and 32 negative w, each exactly representable; fp32 sum of exact integers up to 33*2^20 = 34,603,008 < 2^25, sums up to ~ 2^25*... intermediate partial sums up to ~32*33*2^20 ≈ 1.1e9 < 2^30, exactly representable? Integers up to 2^24 exact; beyond that only multiples of ulp. w values are multiples of 2^20; partial sums are multiples of 2^20, magnitude < 2^30, so representable exactly? multiples of 2^20 up to 2^30: need ulp ≤ 2^20, i.e. magnitude < 2^44 — yes exact. So large sums are exact! Then adding small 0.25 values: when running sum is a multiple of 2^20 in magnitude (e.g. up to 1.1e9), ulp of running sum ≥ 2^(exp-23). For 1e9 ~ 2^30, ulp=64; 0.25 rounds to 0. But permutation order matters: if small values are added early while sum is small, they survive; if sum large, lost. Also when large terms cancel to small residual, previously-lost small terms are gone. So error up to ~ sum of small values lost, per row up to 48. Whether E ≤ 0.1 depends on permutation order. Reference norm: rows sums ~ mean 2*48/... small values 1-3 quarters, sum mean ~64*0.5=... values in {0.25,0.5,0.75}, mean 0.5, sum ~32, norm over 64 rows ~ 32/sqrt... ||ref||_2 ≈ sqrt(64)*~sqrt(var)... roughly 8*sqrt(64*var)... roughly ~ 30-90. Error per row could be tens. Likely fails — Skeptic/Experimenter job. I record description.
